The *Mahākassapattheragāthā* (Thag 18.1) is a major verse text located in the *Theragāthā* collection of the Pali Canon, attributed to the elder Mahākassapa [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, it is indexed with thirteen translations across twelve languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. In later Pali literature, verses or themes from the text are mentioned in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 7.5.6, *Jarasiṅgālaṅgapañha*) [SuttaCentral]. Extensive textual overlap is naturally preserved in the Theragāthā commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, across both parts), which shares extensive text segments with the verses [DharmaNexus].

SuttaCentral notes passage-level parallels in the Pali Nikāyas and verse collections, including AN 11.9 (*Saddhasutta*), SN 22.79 (*Khajjanīyasutta*), Iti 42 (*Sukkadhamma Sutta*), and other poems in the Theragāthā (Thag 8.1 and Thag 2.2), alongside a parallel in the Chinese canon (T 765.87) and a resembling parallel in the Jain *Sūyagaḍaṅgasutta* (Sūyagadamgasuttam 1) [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with SuttaCentral's curated parallel to AN 11.9, computational text reuse from DharmaNexus finds a segment match between verses of this text (§33.4–34.4) and the *Ekādasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
